subject: How to define matrix with varying dimension in a for loop

messages.author: ffb2aff965d4e11b
messages.subject: How to define matrix with varying dimension in a for loop
parts:
Hi Stan,

    I am writing a user-defined posterior density of  a spatial model. Since for each location it uses the nearest neighborhood, the matrix for recording nearest distance has different dimension for different location. What I wrote is 

for (i in 2:N){


           dim = i ? i < (M+1) : M;


           matrix[dim, dim] temp_neardistM;


            for (j in 1:dim){


                for (k in 1:dim){


                    temp_neardistM[j, k] = exp(- phi * neardistM[(i-1), (j-1)*dim + k])+ k == j ? (1/kappa -1): 0.0;

               }

           }


But then I got the error report
SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:

variable "matrix" does not exist.

ERROR at line 16

 14:            for (i in 2:N){
 15:                dim = i ? i < (M+1) : M;
 16:                matrix[dim, dim] temp_neardistM;
                          ^
 17:                for (j in 1:dim){

Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  : 
  failed to parse Stan model 'nngp' due to the above error.

Does anyone have some good suggestion for me? Thanks in advance.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: How to define matrix with varying dimension in a for loop
parts:
On Wednesday, August 24, 2016 at 3:25:22 PM UTC-4, Lu Zhang wrote:
SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:

variable "matrix" does not exist.

ERROR at line 16

 14:            for (i in 2:N){
 15:                dim = i ? i < (M+1) : M;
 16:                matrix[dim, dim] temp_neardistM;
Declarations currently have to happen before any assignments in a block, so it would have to be
for (i in 2:N) {

matrix[i ? i < (M + 1) : M, i ? i < (M + 1): M] temp_neardistM;
  ...
}

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to define matrix with varying dimension in a for loop
parts:
for (i in 2:N){
dim = i ? i < (M+1) : M;

Because i is always non-zero, you always get the first
case of the conditional operator, (i < (M + 1)), which
will evaluate to either 1 or 0 depending on whether
i < M + 1 or not.

- Bob

messages.author: ffb2aff965d4e11b
messages.subject: Re: How to define matrix with varying dimension in a for loop
parts:
Thank you so much! I finally got my code to run. There was also a mistake in my question. The correct code for declaring "dim" should be

dim = (i < (M+1))? (i-1) : M;

On Wednesday, August 24, 2016 at 12:57:05 PM UTC-7, Ben Goodrich wrote:
On Wednesday, August 24, 2016 at 3:25:22 PM UTC-4, Lu Zhang wrote:
SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:

variable "matrix" does not exist.

ERROR at line 16

 14:            for (i in 2:N){
 15:                dim = i ? i < (M+1) : M;
 16:                matrix[dim, dim] temp_neardistM;

Declarations currently have to happen before any assignments in a block, so it would have to be

for (i in 2:N) {
  matrix[i ? i < (M + 1) : M, i ? i < (M + 1): M] temp_neardistM;
  ...
}

Ben
